result.summary:
All six AS1 models exist, the validator is green and every budget holds (all numbers measured on software OpenGL). The showroom flag stays false for both player cars: the real-time picture has the richer mesh, but its paint and lighting are flatter than the Cycles sprite.

- Player cars (limousine, kompakt): race level, show level and shadow caster. Lamps are recesses with depth; glass is transparent and tinted over a dark interior; the rear has a third brake light, plate frame with plate lamps, exhaust tips and badge; the front has grille depth, wipers and antenna.
- Traffic cars (sedan, hatch, wagon): rebuilt on the smooth SmoothCar lofts. Windows, lamps and plates are cut in along their contours, so lod0, lod1 and lod2 share the same outlines and nothing crumples. All colour sets are paint values of one mesh.
- Truck: tractor and box trailer as node groups with pivots, four liveries as paint. The rear reads at 20, 60 and 150 m, day and night.
- Late fix: the dark hatching on the kompakt in the showroom A/B came from the shadow caster, not the mesh. The coarse hull stood 7.9 mm out of the body and its wheel caps shaded the rims. Hulls are now tucked 12 mm inside the skin.

Gates: sprite geometry 187 of 187 identical, full test run passed, Arcade 20 von 20 identisch, model render check OK. The tests ran one commit before HEAD; that last commit only adds an export guard and documentation, and a forced re-export afterwards left every model file byte-identical.

deviations: Traffic cars are built on the carbody.SmoothCar lofts instead of the vehicles.Car lofts, which crumpled at lod1/lod2 and let bumpers poke through. Dimensions, windows and lamps still come from cesprites.designs.
The truck is a new 3D builder (ce3d/truck3d.py) using the dimensions of cesprites.heavy, not the box generator of the sprites.
One truck mesh serves all four liveries through paint, paint2 and paint3; there is no tarp variant for red and green.
Traffic lod2 drops plate, reverse light, daytime running light and sill split to stay inside 1,200 triangles; tail, brake, indicator and head lamps keep their contours.
Player chase pictures are taken at 9 m and 30 m instead of 8 m: at 8 m the rear bumper is below the screen edge of the game camera.
tests_total counts 569 unit tests plus 64 CHECK lines of the one complete run.
contract_issues: PREMUL_ALPHA_FACTOR does not exist in the GLES3 scene shader of Godot 4.7.2 (compile error: premul_alpha undeclared). The glass uses blend_premul_alpha and premultiplies itself.

glass.gdshader: the render_mode line (now blend_premul_alpha, depth_draw_never, cull_back) is shared between AS1 (look) and R3, so a merge conflict is possible. The instance uniforms fade and sun and the light() function are untouched.

Grouped node names (tractor/body, trailer/wheel_0l) and the manifest key groups (pivots of tractor and trailer) are new. ModelFactory builds the parts but does not read groups, so the truck does not articulate yet.

The contract says nothing about where the shadow caster lies. A caster outside the body skin shades its own body; the models now keep it 12 mm inside (truck 30 mm). The export stops if a car hull is not inside, but validate_models.py has no rule for it yet.
notes_for_next: R3 paint shader: the cars need a clear coat with Fresnel and environment reflection over a slightly darker base tone. This is the main gap to the Cycles sprites; metallic flakes are optional after that.

R3: rims and chrome (metallic 0.55-1.0, roughness 0.12-0.3) need an environment to reflect. Ambient occlusion and a contact shadow under the car must come from the renderer; no vertex channel is free for it.

R3: the lit lamp parts sit up to 28 mm behind an almost clear lens (opacity 0.08-0.10) which must not darken them. Light anchors lie in the opening of the recess, up to 33 mm in front of the lit geometry.

Renderer: tail lamps of a truck at 150 m at night are about two pixels; the glow at the light anchors (fairness rule F6) has to carry them. The truck also has two marker anchors on top of the trailer.
RINT/R3: to articulate the truck, read groups from the manifest and turn the trailer/* parts about the trailer pivot [0, 1.19, -3.7] and the tractor about [0, 0, -3.1].

Showroom flag: once the paint shader and the showroom light exist, repeat tools/models_contact_sheet.sh <png> --only="player/*" --showroom. If real-time is at least equal, set "showroom": True for showroom/limousine and showroom/kompakt in tools/blender/ce3d/catalog3d.py and run export_models.py --manifest-only.

Art review, weakest model-side points: traffic lamps are flat cut-in fields without lens or depth, the traffic rear is a nearly vertical face with a plain bumper and block-shaped plate characters, and lod2 has triangular wheel cut-outs with hexagonal wheels.
Art review, further weak points: rims are simple, player headlights show little depth from ahead, door handles are small brackets, and the truck cab is a flat profile body without interior.
AS2a/AS2b: new car bodies can reuse traffic3d (smooth_design, CAR_3D) and core.tuck_inside for shadow casters. Lod0 budgets are tight: the wagon has 112 triangles left of 18,000.
CE_STATS=1 before an export prints triangles per object and per decal projection without changing files. docs/modelle.md section 13 describes the vehicle pipeline.
result.quality_verdict:
What the player sees is clearly better than the wave-0 reference cars, but it is not yet the 'detailreiche Grafik' the wish describes, and the main reason is shading, not mesh.

Good: the player cars have taut bodies with crisp panel gaps, lamp clusters with real depth, transparent tinted glass over a visible interior, a worked-out rear and front, and rims that now catch sunlight. From the chase camera at 9 m the rear reads cleanly by day and night. Traffic cars keep exactly the same silhouette and lamp outlines at all three levels; brake light and amber indicator are unmistakable at 8, 30 and 80 m. The truck rear reads at once from 20 to 150 m.

Not yet good: the paint looks like bright plastic, with no clear coat, no environment reflections and no ambient occlusion. In the same-camera showroom A/B the Cycles sprite still looks more natural, so the showroom flag stays false for both cars. Traffic cars are clean but plain up close: flat lamps without lenses, a flat rear with a bare bumper, no interior. Traffic lod2 is angular and meant for beyond 120 m. Rims are simple; the truck cab has no curved front and no interior; one trailer mesh serves all four liveries.

Missing or unproven: clear-coat paint shader and contact shadows (R3), showroom lighting (UI1), truck articulation in ModelFactory. Everything was rendered on software OpenGL through the contact-sheet rig; how it looks in the real race renderer, on a Steam Deck or on a real GPU is inferred, not measured.

result.summary:
Engine v3 for the sound profile Modern is in place. The slots EngineAudio3 and VehicleLayers have real content (class names, hooks, state()/perf()/preview(id) kept). tools/audio/modern/engine_synth3.py generates five stereo cycle banks (format ce-engine-bank-2: overrun / load-without-induction / induction layer per rpm point) and twelve natively mixed vehicle sounds from the frozen physical model (imported, not edited). EngineBank2 loads them through ModernAudioAssets.read_i16(); EngineMixThread mixes in a worker thread (synchronous for --audio-sync or engine_thread=false) with power-true blends, fast and slow random movement, saturation, clips and limiter; VehicleLayers adds turbo tone and hiss, driveline whine, tip-in, shift thump, blow-off. levels.MSfx is now 0 dB.

Measured (dev VM, headless, Dummy driver): full throttle -16.0 to -17.1 LUFS, idle -23.5 to -25.1, cruise -20.9 to -22.3 (with the stand-in wind); 0 underruns with six 400 ms hitches (main-thread mixing: 345-427); 20 of 20 shutdowns exit 0; sync mode bit-identical twice; 0.78-0.94 ms mixing per 1/60 s of sound; audio_qc with determinism green; golden 20 von 20.

Tests: full run 1 green (595 tests, all checks). Full run 2 hit one randomness-dependent test of my own; fixed, and the whole unit phase is green on the final commit. No third full run (rule), so the integration scenarios were not repeated on the final commit.

Nobody listened. A/B MP3s, spectrograms and numbers per car are in the deliver folder. Honest limits: same physical model as Arcade; the engine is dry and sits in the centre for the three inline engines (in-game L/R correlation 0.97-1.00, Arcade with its reverb 0.80-0.99). Predecessor's branch and worktree were continued.

contract_issues: tools/audio/modern/modern_lib.py (AU-A): write_wav_import() and write_ogg_import() open the .import file for writing (lines 118 / 128) before _import_head() reads it - every regeneration loses uid and import path and the game reports 'Failed loading resource' until godot --import has run. Worked around in engine_synth3.write_wav_import_keep(); the fix belongs in modern_lib.py.

Godot 4.7.2: a looping AudioStreamWAV whose loop ends with its data plays one wrong frame at every seam (measured with a loop of the constant 0.5: one frame near 0 per seam at pitch 1 and 0.77; none with 16 continuation frames behind loop_end). Consequences: a faint click on tonal loops and two --audio-sync Movie Maker runs differing in 49 sample values. My loops carry the continuation; the placeholders and future loops of AU-C1/C2 do not - needs one place in modern_lib.py and a rule in audio_qc.py. Not examined for the loops the frozen Arcade code builds at run time.

'20 clean shutdowns' cannot mean a silent log: Godot prints 'ObjectDB instances were leaked at exit' / 'resources still in use at exit' whenever a process ends while any AudioStreamPlayer plays (reproduced without Modern code; with stop() before quit() nothing is printed). Clean = exit code 0 and no other message.

ModernAudioFrame.alive (0.35 s): one long frame looks like a session that is gone. '0 underruns with 400 ms hitches' therefore needs a grace rule in every module that should play through; engine and layers use EngineAudio3.driven(), other slots (road, wind) will dip for a frame after a hitch. The rule belongs in ModernAudioFrame.
A-5 says the idle and cruise targets 'can only be met by AU-B's engine': they are met against the stand-in wind; the sums also depend on AU-C1's road and wind and must be measured again then.

The acceptance 'full throttle -16 +/- 1.5 LUFS short-term' is met by phase loudness, short-term median and maximum, but not by every single 3-s window of a pull from standstill (Limousine -18.2 in the low gears, -14.8 at top speed with the wind at 250 km/h). The contract does not say which statistic counts.

Thread measurements exist only for the Dummy driver (blocks of about 93 ms, which made a start prefill and a remembered block size necessary). Behaviour on a real driver and on the Steam Deck is inferred.

result.quality_verdict:
Nobody has heard this engine; everything below is measured or read from spectrograms, and how it sounds is inferred.

Good, measured: the five cars now sit within 1.6 dB of each other on the loudness plan (Arcade: up to 11 dB apart); the sound never stands still at constant speed (1-s level moves by 0.5-0.65 dB instead of 0.01-0.04, no measurable repetition); induction follows the pedal and the exhaust follows the load; the pure 5-6 kHz sine whistle of Arcade (a tenth of the power on the Kompakt) is replaced by a quieter narrow-band tone with flow noise; harmonic series under load are denser; the mixer thread plays through 400 ms hitches without a dropout. The five characters differ clearly in numbers (centroid at 85 % of redline from 350 Hz for the Kompakt to 1429 Hz for the Sportwagen, HNR 5 to 12 dB, two cars with real left/right content).

Not yet good or unknown: it is the same physical model as Arcade, so the basic voice is related and the spectrograms look alike; the Limousine's pull is the least changed. The engine is dry and centred for Kompakt, Kombi and Limousine - by channel correlation the Arcade engine with its reverb is wider in the game. Low rpm under full load is still bass-heavy (a 180 Hz high-pass takes 13-14 dB there, small speakers inferred), the Limousine remains a tonal drone at 200 km/h, the Sportwagen is noisier at the top than in Arcade, the idle ticks stand out more without reverb. Levels of turbo, whine and shift thumps follow laws and pictures, not ears; I softened the shift thump twice after seeing it in the captures.

Missing: a listening pass, a real audio device, the final road and wind around it.
